principles: Preserve cryptographic invariants absolutely: signature salts containing koala are frozen constants, never renamed — verified mechanically (git diff salt-grep + test:koala-residue salt exemption) after every change.
Code is the source of truth for what is removable; docs (CLAUDE.md, decisions/) are reconciled TO the code, not vice versa.
Change allowlist DATA, never enforcement LOGIC: the koala-residue gate stays green by tightening exemptions, not by weakening checks.
One checklist item at a time with build + test:koala-residue + tsc + salt-grep between items (high blast radius demands incremental verification).
Conservative GC: remove only genuinely-dead code (confirmed no consumer); keep every legacy-JSON-compat @deprecated field with an annotated rationale.
drivers: OSS launch needs a clean repo: no stale koala branding/URLs and no dead backward-compat fallback.

Catastrophic downside if a salt is renamed (every signed gate artifact in every repo bricks) — outweighs all cleanup benefit; the plan is optimized to make a salt rename impossible to commit silently.
dev-memory already migrated to ~/.lattice + health.jsonl obsolete → removing the .koala read fallback is genuinely data-safe.

options.name: clean-break-preserve-salts
pros: Removes the .koala read-fallback + non-salt koala identifiers + package.json URLs + dead dispatch aliases while preserving all salts verbatim.
Keeps test:koala-residue green by only tightening allowlist DATA.
Conservative @deprecated GC keeps legacy-JSON-compat fields; only deletes annotations on the deleted aliases.
Incremental per-item verification + salt-grep makes a salt rename impossible to ship unnoticed.
cons: Intentional backward-compat DROP: external repos still on .koala/ would break (accepted — OSS clean break; this repo + fleet are on .lattice).
High file count (11 fallback files + residue script + 2 package.json + CLAUDE.md + dispatch files) means more review surface.

options.name: total-removal-rename-salts
pros: Total koala removal including salts means zero koala anywhere.
cons: CATASTROPHIC: renaming salts invalidates every existing signed init-check/delivery-check/scope-check/draft-check/finding artifact in every repo. Explicitly REJECTED by the user.

options.name: keep-fallback-no-op
pros: Zero risk: keep the .koala read fallback as-is.
cons: Leaves dead backward-compat + stale koala branding/URLs in the OSS repo; user explicitly wants the clean break and the data is already migrated.

rationale: clean-break-preserve-salts is the only option satisfying the users explicit directive (clean OSS koala cleanup) while honoring the non-negotiable salt-preservation constraint. total-removal-rename-salts is catastrophic and user-rejected; keep-fallback-no-op leaves the repo dirty against the users wishes. The chosen option is made safe by: per-item incremental verification, a salt-grep against /tmp/salt-baseline-B-a4e3.txt after every change, keeping the koala-residue gate green (which via its surviving salt exemption proves salts are intact), and conservative @deprecated GC that preserves legacy-JSON-compat fields. story_dispatch/finding_dispatch are both confirmed deprecated by docs/requirements/decisions/cli-engine-english-open-source-execution-plan.md (B-9d95 CHK-004 merged both into lattice dispatch); the command-policy story_dispatch status:supported is a stale mislabel deleted alongside the alias.

preMortem.scenario: An implementer renames a koala-* signature salt (e.g. koala-init-check-integrity-v1 to lattice-init-check-integrity-v1) while sweeping koala identifiers, treating it as branding.
preMortem.trigger: CHK-002 instructs renaming non-salt koala identifiers; an implementer over-applies the rename to a salt literal because both contain the substring koala.
preMortem.consequence: CATASTROPHIC: every existing signed init-check / delivery-check / scope-check / draft-check / finding artifact in every repo fails signature verification — all gates brick, no story can advance.
preMortem.mitigation: (1) Every implementer prompt opens with the explicit frozen-salt list + DO-NOT-RENAME constraint. (2) Salt files are NOT in execution_boundary allowedPaths. (3) After every implementer dispatch, main agent runs git diff main HEAD piped to grep for koala integrity/salt patterns and diffs the 25-line salt baseline at /tmp/salt-baseline-B-a4e3.txt — must show ZERO modified salt lines, else REVERT immediately. (4) test:koala-residue salt exemption (line 81) staying green is independent mechanical proof. (5) REVIEW reviewers are told to verify no salt was renamed.

preMortem.scenario: Tightening the verify-koala-residue.mjs allowlist removes an exemption that is still needed, turning the gate RED (false positive) — or an implementer edits the gates enforcement logic instead of just its allowlist data.
preMortem.trigger: CHK-002 shrinks the allowlist; an implementer drops the salt exemption (line 81) or a still-referenced legacy path exemption, or refactors the scanning logic.
preMortem.consequence: test:koala-residue goes red and blocks REVIEW→TEST, or (worse) the gate is weakened so real koala residue passes undetected.
preMortem.mitigation: Run npm run test:koala-residue after EVERY allowlist edit and require PASS koala-residue: 0 unclassified. Constraint: only change allowlist DATA arrays, never the scan/classify functions. Keep line 81 salt exemption + all historical/doc exemptions; only drop exemptions whose target path literal no longer exists after the fallback removal. Reviewer verifies the diff touches only allowlist arrays.

preMortem.scenario: An implementer deletes a legacy-JSON-compat @deprecated field (e.g. ChecklistItem.testIntent, TestResult.git) thinking it is dead, breaking deserialization of old stored story JSON.
preMortem.trigger: CHK-005 GCs @deprecated fields; an implementer deletes one that still has a reader in the old-JSON parse path.
preMortem.consequence: Old stories fail to load / lose data; lattice validate or story reads throw at runtime on existing repos.
preMortem.mitigation: All 7 @deprecated symbols are pre-classified KEEP (investigation confirmed each has a live reader or is exported+tested). CHK-005 scope is narrowed to ONLY removing the dead dispatch alias methods + their JSDoc @deprecated annotations + their command-policy/registry entries — NOT type fields. Implementer prompt explicitly lists the KEEP set with rationale. tsc + the full battery (incl. flow-stability-smoke + dev-memory-legacy-read-smoke) must stay green; any compat break surfaces as a test failure.

preMortem.scenario: Removing a LEGACY_KOALA_DIR fallback branch breaks a consumer that silently depended on the .koala read path at runtime (e.g. planner.ts reading .koala/planner/runs).
preMortem.trigger: CHK-001 removes the fallback in 10 consumer files; one consumer had no .lattice equivalent wired and only ever read .koala.
preMortem.consequence: That feature (e.g. planner run history, autopilot-runs) silently returns empty / throws on repos that only had .koala data.
preMortem.mitigation: For each of the 10 consumers, the implementer must confirm the .lattice canonical path is the live write target (LATTICE_* constant exists) before deleting the .koala branch, and that this repo has zero .koala data (verified). The dev-memory-legacy-read-smoke.ts is flipped to assert .koala is no longer read (proving removal). Full battery + tsc green; reviewer checks each consumer keeps a working .lattice path.
